stem: A 68-year-old woman comes to the office due to painful urination with increased urinary frequency and urgency for the past 2 days.  She has had 4 similar episodes over the last 3 years that resolved with oral antibiotic therapy.  Urine cultures from these previous occasions have grown Escherichia coli.  The patient has no chronic medical conditions and takes no daily medications.  Menopause was at age 52.  Vital signs are normal.  Physical examination shows mild suprapubic tenderness.  There is no costovertebral angle tenderness.  Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria.  Postvoid residual volume is 35 mL (normal: <50).  Which of the following is most likely contributing to this patient's recurrent urinary infections?​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​​
explanation:
This patient with multiple episodes of urinary urgency, pyuria, and bacteriuria has had recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs).  Risk factors for recurrent UTIs include behavioral (eg, new sexual partner, spermicide use), anatomic (eg, presence of cystocele, urinary incontinence), and biologic (eg, menopause) factors.  This postmenopausal patient most likely has genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), which is characterized by bothersome genital and urinary symptoms resulting from hypoestrogenism.

Menopause dramatically decreases estrogen levels, which results in thin vaginal epithelium, loss of rugation, decreased vaginal secretions, and low epithelial glycogen content.  Because Lactobacilli species (the dominant vaginal flora in premenopausal women) normally use glycogen as a substrate for lactic acid production, the low glycogen content associated with GSM causes vaginal pH to increase.  These combined factors promote a vaginal flora shift characterized by colonization with skin or rectal flora, which predisposes to recurrent UTIs.  Additionally, the urinary tract also has estrogen receptors and is affected by diminishing estrogen.  Subsequent urinary tract atrophy further predisposes patients to recurrent UTIs.

Vaginal estrogen is effective for both atrophy and prevention of UTIs.

(Choice A)  Acquired vesicoureteral reflux develops due to increased pressure in the bladder, typically from bladder outlet obstruction or neurogenic bladder.  Patients typically have abnormally elevated postvoid residual volumes and costovertebral angle tenderness due to hydronephrosis, which are not seen in this patient.

(Choice B)  Increasing age is associated with a decrease in the total number of B cells; however, immunoglobin levels remain relatively unchanged despite some drop in antibody diversity and quality.  Furthermore, secretory IgA (not IgG) is the most important antibody for mucosal defense of the urinary tract.

(Choice C)  Decreased antibacterial efficacy occurs when bacteria develop resistance to antibiotics.  Patients with recurrent UTIs are at risk if they receive frequent, repeated courses of antibiotics or daily antibiotic prophylaxis.  This patient has had only 4 infections in the last 3 years and each episode resolved appropriately with treatment, making antibiotic resistance less likely.

(Choice E)  Vaccine-induced immunity does wane with time as IgG levels drop.  However, there are no vaccines that protect against organisms that commonly cause UTIs (eg, Escherichia coli, Group B Streptococcus, Enterococci, Klebsiella, Proteus).

Educational objective:Menopause and associated low estrogen levels can lead to genitourinary syndrome of menopause, which predisposes patients to recurrent urinary tract infections due to atrophy and shifts in vaginal flora.​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​​
